warning: All five are source-interpretation investigations; even a documented arithmetic explanation is not an independent medical/statistical signoff, RAAS grade, FDA probability or retrospective point-in-time prediction.

cases.title: Ataluren vs placebo — Week 48 percent-predicted FEV1
cases.rawObservation: Saved trial arm means -2.534 and -5.500 yield unadjusted subtraction 2.966; reported 2.7540 (95% CI -0.756 to 6.264; p=0.1235) is a least-squares adjusted effect. The matching official EU clinical-trial results identify an MMRM adjusted for baseline FEV1, treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit, baseline-by-visit and stratification factors.
cases.interpretation: The original EU registry results explicitly distinguish raw means from the least-squares mixed-model estimate. Subtracting unadjusted arms is therefore not a direct reconstruction of the modeled 2.754 contrast; the observed 0.212 gap is not evidence of a registry arithmetic error or a favorable clinical outcome. Exact model replication from patient-level data remains unavailable.
cases.neededBeforeClosure: For independent signoff, verify the EU and ClinicalTrials.gov source identity, MMRM specification, intention-to-treat population, missing-data treatment and adjusted estimand. The source supports a method-based explanation, not an authenticated RAAS grade.

cases.title: KamRAB vs HRIG — Day 14 anti-rabies antibody threshold
cases.rawObservation: The registry compact index shows 55 and 58 responders (counts) but the reported -0.018 is a difference in proportions. The FDA clinical review describes 55/56 in the KamRAB group and 58/58 in the comparator group; 55/56 minus 58/58 equals approximately -0.017857, which rounds to -0.018.
cases.interpretation: The numerical discrepancy was a unit/denominator mismatch in the old raw-count subtraction, not evidence that the original trial results are inconsistent. This reproducible arithmetic does not independently certify clinical non-inferiority.
cases.neededBeforeClosure: Preserve the exact as-treated denominators and the FDA review's 90% confidence-interval/non-inferiority analysis. Require independent adjudication for any RAAS metric.

cases.title: NKTR-181 vs placebo — weekly pain score change
cases.rawObservation: The displayed arm scores are 0.9 and 1.5 (one decimal place), yielding -0.6 by direct subtraction, versus a saved reported contrast of -0.55 (p=0.0019). Two arm values rounded to tenths can together shift a difference by up to approximately 0.10, so the 0.05 gap is rounding-compatible.
cases.interpretation: Displayed precision is insufficient to establish a real contrast discrepancy. Statistical adjustment and the exact estimand still require source review; this is not independent efficacy verification.
cases.neededBeforeClosure: Inspect the original trial statistical analysis and unrounded outcome estimates if a precise treatment-effect reconciliation is required.

cases.title: A-101 vs vehicle — common wart clearance Day 60
cases.rawObservation: The primary outcome stores five measurements for each OG treatment group across wart-number classes: treatment 40,33,2,2,3 and vehicle 13,10,1,1,1. The prior code retained only the last pair (3 and 1), then incorrectly compared its difference 2 with the model-reported 3.22.
cases.interpretation: A repeated OG identifier does not identify a single comparable analysis row. The compact source omits the class labels; 3.22 cannot be re-derived by subtracting an arbitrary group pair. This is a source-flattening interpretation problem, not proven clinical inconsistency.
cases.neededBeforeClosure: Retain class-level labels from the full original ClinicalTrials.gov outcome measure and verify model type, population denominators and analysis statistic.

cases.title: AL001 vs placebo — symptomatic FTD CDR plus NACC FTLD-SB
cases.rawObservation: The source index contains three pairs for the same OG IDs: 9.686/8.177, 6.765/5.771 and 4.477/4.628. The prior code kept only the last pair (-0.151) while the reported mean-difference statistic is 1.509. The first saved pair has arithmetic difference exactly 1.509.
cases.interpretation: The match of 1.509 to the first pair is a strong lead that the old mismatch came from overwritten repeated observations. Because the compact index omits time-point/class labels, this does not establish which pair belongs to the reported comparison. Do not claim efficacy or FDA outcome based on this arithmetic.
cases.neededBeforeClosure: Inspect complete original 48/72/96-week outcome classes and the statistical analysis plan to identify the prespecified model, endpoint time and estimated contrast.
